full_judgment: 4. The respondent filed Other Suit No. 68 of 1982 against the appellant and 3 others for a declaration that the agreement for sale of the suit property dated 8-8-79 was illegal, void, inoperative, not binding upon him and not enforceable against him and the respondent be given a decree for khas possession of the suit property against the appellant and also for a decree for Taka 67,500.00 as compensation on the allegations, inter alia, that a vacant residential plot or Chittagong Co-operative Housing Society was purchased from Haji Md. Mabud by three separate documents, one by the respondent's father in his name and the others by his maternal uncle and maternal aunt in 1975, that as the document stood in the name of the plaintiff the building was constructed on taking House Building loan by mortgaging the property with House Building Finance Corporation by a registered mortgage deed dated 19-12-77 but the loan amount was insufficient and his father made contribution for constructing the house which was completed in 1978 at a cost of Taka 5,00,000.00, that the respondent himself supervised the construction of the building which was a well built and well designed house as it was intended for personal occupation being the only house to live in, that the cost or construction of the house exceeded the estimate as best materials were used, as a result of which there was heavy outstanding dues to different creditors, like supplies of materials, masons, carpenters, etc who were pressing vary hard for payment of their dues but neither the respondent nor his father could arrange for fund for clearing the dues and his father became very annoyed as he spent a lot of money beyond the estimate and used to rebuke him, as a result of which the respondent became very much mentally upset, that the father of the appellant is a very shrewd man who promised to procure a good and solvent tenant for the respondent who would be able to pay heavy advance but after a few days the father of the appellant advised him to dispose of the building and being in necessity of money the respondent agreed to sell the suit property to the appellant, that the respondent was not in a position to make bargain due to his age and inexperience and as a result of which the negotiation was one-sided and the purchaser got the upper hand in the deal between unequals; that the respondent was not prepared to put the appellant in possession of the suit property till the full payment of the price but the appellant insisted upon delivery of possession at the time of execution of the agreement, that without considering the interest of the respondent the appellant exercised undue influence and duress in the matter of preparing the sale agreement, that the agreement was executed and drawn up in the name of the appellant wherein the price was fixed at Taka 5,50,000.00 of which Taka 3,00,000.00 was to be paid on the date of agreement and out of the balance she should pay Taka 1,67,000.00 to the House Building Finance Corporation and Taka 83,000.00 to the respondent and the transaction shall have to be completed within 31st January, 1980, and time was the essence of contract, that if she fails to pay the balance of consideration money within the stipulated time the earnest money shall stand forfeited and she shall vacate the premises at once, that the respondent had to accept the terms of the agreement and to hand over the possession of the suit property before the registration of the sale deed and payment of full price under very compelling circumstances, that after getting into possession of the suit property the appellant became very much callous and she failed to complete the transaction within the stipulated time and made default both in the matter of payment of the instalments of House Building loan to the House Building Finance Corporation as well as to pay the balance consideration money within the stipulated time, that the agreement between the parties had expired by efflux of time on 31st January, 1980 due to default of the appellant, that the agreement for sale was void and not enforceable as no approval was obtained from the House Building Finance Corporation before the agreement, that the respondent cancelled the agreement by a legal notice dated 30-6-1980 and asked the appellant to vacate the suit house within one month from the date of the notice in default the earnest money would be forfeited, that the respondent was served with a notice by the House Building Finance Corporation for payment of outstanding dues and he had to deposit a sum of Taka 20,000.00 with the House Building Finance Corporation on 6-4-80, that with a malafide intention the appellant insisted upon the respondent to pay the House Building loan contrary to the terms of the agreement by serving a notice just before the expiry of the stipulated period and that the respondent and his parents have got no other house in the Chittagong city excepting the suit house and, as such, it would be great hardship unless the possession of the suit house is given back to him as he and his parents have no other house to live in; that the appellant violated the order of ad-interim injunction passed against her restraining her from making any construction for which he filed Miscellaneous Case No. 134 of 1982, that the respondent has been paying the instalments of House Building loan and also paying the rent and municipal taxes regularly and that the respondent was entitled to get Taka 67,000.00 as compensation for use and occupation of the suit house by the appellant.
